o1.biggest_strength: Sharpest read of the store's own numbers: it names that the $24,000 label-read opener was the worst performer, builds all three scripts to open on taste, and adds a cut-rule test plan plus creator rights and deliverables.
o1.biggest_mistake: It overloads the shared rules block and test plan, so the doc is denser and slower to scan than it needs to be for a small team.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Put a one-line disclosure/deliverables header on each script and trim wording so it scans in seconds.

o2.biggest_strength: Cleanest, most natural spoken scripts — hooks like "It's 3 pm. You know what that means." and beats like "And one for me" read aloud beautifully and stay on brand.
o2.biggest_mistake: The scripts carry no spoken paid-partnership disclosure (only an #ad caption and platform toggles) and the briefs skip deliverable and rights specs, leaving compliance and production homework.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add an on-camera "Olipop paid me" line to each script and put deliverables, safe zones and rights into each creator brief.

reason: Both are shootable and on brand, but Output 1 catches the real money signal (label reads wasted the most spend), writes spoken disclosure into the scripts, and hands the team a test plan and rights terms they can run with tomorrow; Output 2 is cleaner but lighter on insight and compliance.
